title: Control of gene expression: transcription factors and epigenetics; Principles of homeostasis and negative feedback
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: HO01#t3 term and clue written for the game; HO01#t4 term and clue written for the game; HO01#t1 term and clue written for the game; GR01b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GR01b#N.4, HO01#N.4b, GR01b#N.12, HO01#N.7c.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Receptor
items.clue: Part of a control loop that detects the stimulus.

items.label: Effector
items.clue: Muscle or gland that makes the response in a control loop.

items.label: Homeostasis
items.clue: Keeping the internal environment within limits, whatever happens outside.

items.label: Epigenetic tags
items.clue: Marks added or removed by diet, stress or pollution; they alter phenotype, not base sequence.

questions.stem: Blood cells from people living in a city with high levels of particulate air pollution were compared with blood cells from people living in an area with clean air. The pattern of methyl tags on the DNA of several genes differed between the two groups, but the base sequences of those genes were the same. Which conclusion is best supported by these findings?

options.text: The two groups must have differed genetically before any exposure to pollution
Air pollution acted as a mutagen, changing the genes in the blood cells
Air pollution altered gene expression without altering genotype
The altered tags will be inherited by the children of the exposed people

questions.explanation: Altered methyl tags with an unchanged base sequence is an environmental effect on gene expression: the expression pattern changed while the genotype did not.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the feedback mechanisms that maintain an organism's internal environment?

options.text: They keep each internal condition at one exact value, which does not vary from moment to moment.
They act at the level of the whole organism, but not between molecules or within cells.
They respond to changes caused by the organism's own activity and to changes in its surroundings.
They are called negative when they harm the organism and positive when they help it.

questions.explanation: Feedback mechanisms respond to internal changes, such as heat produced by working muscles, and external changes, such as a fall in air temperature.

questions.stem: Female honeybee larvae in a hive are genetically alike. Larvae fed only on royal jelly develop into fertile queens; larvae switched to a diet of worker jelly develop into smaller, sterile workers. Which explanation is consistent with the understanding of gene expression?

options.text: Larvae fed worker jelly lose the genes that are needed for queen development
The diet alters epigenetic tags, so the two castes express different sets of the same genes
Royal jelly contains a mutagen that alters the base sequence of the larva's growth genes
The diet cannot cause the difference, so the caste of each larva must be fixed at fertilisation

questions.stem: In a person whose pancreas does not release insulin, which prediction about blood glucose concentration after a meal containing carbohydrate is best supported?

options.text: It returns to the set point as fast as normal, as the body adjusts to meet its own need.
It rises and stays high longer than usual, as the response that lowers it is missing.
It stays at exactly the set point, as homeostasis keeps blood glucose at a fixed value.
It falls below the set point, as glucagon, which lowers blood glucose, is still released.
